data.title: BAE Systems scores European combat vehicle contracts worth $6B
data.description:
BAE Systems (BAESY) (BAESF) said Friday it was awarded contracts worth a combined $6B (€5.5B) for the delivery of more than 400 CV90 combat vehicles to Finland, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway, and Sweden, as increased European defense spending turns into orders.

The countries signed the joint procurement for the vehicle, made by BAE Systems Hägglunds in ​Sweden, in ⁠Stockholm on Friday.

The joint procurement shows the "dramatic change" in how European countries are approaching defense since the start of Russia's war against Ukraine, BAE Systems Hägglunds general manager Tommy Gustafsson-Rask told Bloomberg in an interview.

Countries are now putting in more money and "talking to each other, talking about demand, finding the smart solutions, doing things jointly," Gustafsson-Rask said.

Earlier this month, BAE Systems (BAESY) (BAESF) raised its annual free cash flow guidance by nearly 50%, and the company said it has seen an increase in orders as Europe buys weapons to bolster their militaries and reduce their dependence on the U.S.

data.title: Wall Street climbs higher on Black Friday
data.description:
Wall Street climbed higher on Black Friday as major indices posted gains following the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week, with traders reassessing positions amid lighter trading volumes.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +0.8%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, nine of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with energy leading the way higher, while health care has been the weakest area. 

Moreover, the economic calendar remains light for the session as the U.S. stock markets will close early on Friday for the Black Friday holiday session. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) added 2 basis points to 4.66%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) shifted up 3 basis points to 4.89%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) moved higher by 4 basis points to 5.29%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Sandisk (SNDK) advanced +8.5%, while shares of Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) dropped -9.3%.

data.title: AI bubble debate: Drawing parallels with the dot-com era
data.description:
The recent tech selloff has revived a question that markets have been avoiding: will the AI bubble finally burst?

Investors have been worried about the massive investments being poured in to fund the AI buildout and when they will pay off.

Venture money is already shrinking: global AI funding totaled $103.3B in Q3, according to market intelligence platform CB Insights. That's down from Q2's $153.1B and Q1's $226B.

To note, Q2's tally was driven largely by Anthropic's (ANT) three mega-rounds totaling $65B and OpenAI's (OPENAI) $122B raise accounted for over half of AI funding during Q1.

Meanwhile, companies continue to spend heavily on AI. Goldman Sachs estimated that companies will invest ~$1T globally in AI this year, with just under $600B in the U.S. alone. 

There are many parallels that can be drawn with the dot-com era, like the pick-and-shovel plays and circular financing trends.

A pick-and-shovel play — a term that emerged from the California Gold Rush — is an investment strategy that focuses on companies supplying infrastructure or services within an industry, instead of investing in the end products.

Nvidia (NVDA) is an example of a pick-and-shovel bet in the AI trade, just as Cisco (CSCO) and Lucent — once among the most valuable companies in early 2000 — were during the dot-com era.

Shares of Lucent lost nearly all their value during the dot-com crash, while Cisco's (CSCO) stock lost ~80%-90% of its value.

AI circular financing, another major concern, refers to chipmakers and cloud firms investing in or lending to AI labs and neocloud operators, which commit to buying chips or compute back from the same companies.

"What we are seeing is more akin to a sophisticated vendor-financing structure, but at an extraordinary scale," FTSE Russell analysts noted. "A closer analogue may be the Telcom buildout in the late-1990s, where modelling of future demand led to overinvestment in infrastructure."

Back then, larger telecom equipment makers like Cisco (CSCO), Lucent and Nortel offered cash-strapped customers financing deals so they could buy the vendors' hardware. This, in turn, fueled rapid infrastructure buildouts… Sounds familiar?

AI buildout investments will total $10.3T from 2025 to 2032, or an average of 3.63% of U.S. GDP per year, according to a recent report published by the Brookings Institution. That's a lot bigger than past investment booms in U.S. railroads, highways, and telecom.

But unlike the dot-com era, the biggest spenders in the AI era are some of the most profitable companies ever. That cushion may be thinning, with Meta's (META) free cash flow turning negative in Q3 for the first time in 14 years.

Here are some notable stocks in the AI trade:

AI software: (ANT), (PLTR), (AI), (SOUN), (BBAI), (APLD), (TEM).

AI chips: (NVDA), (AMD), (AVGO), (MRVL), (QCOM), (INTC), (ARM), (MU), (TSM), (GFS).

Cloud computing, hyperscalers: (MSFT), (AMZN), (GOOG) (GOOGL), (META), (ORCL), (IBM), (CRWV), (NBIS), (NET).

data.title: Vertex falls on “disappointing” FDA delay on kidney drug review; Vera rises
data.description:
Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) traded lower on Friday, and rival Vera Therapeutics (VERA) gained after the U.S. FDA extended its review of the former’s kidney disease drug povetacicept, a decision Leerink Partners identified as “quite disappointing.”

Announcing the revised Feb. 28 target action date issued in connection with its Biologics License Application for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy, Vertex (VRTX) on Wednesday attributed the delay to an information request from the FDA.

The company's stock lost more than 10% after the announcement, its worst intra-day performance since August 2025.

Vera Therapeutics (VERA), whose once-weekly injectable branded as Trutakna received the U.S. accelerated approval for IgA nephropathy in July, added ~15% in reaction, recording its best intraday gain since June 2025.

Noting the review extension as “quite disappointing,” Leerink Partners analyst David Risinger, who has an Outperform rating on Vertex (VRTX), remained hopeful. “We now assume that pove will be approved within the next three months,” Risinger wrote, according to Bloomberg.“Although we cannot predict the FDA label, we are hoping that if blood monitoring is required, it is infrequent and thus does not materially impact commercial prospects,” the analyst added.

Baird analyst Brian Skorney, who has an Underperform rating on Vertex (VRTX), argued that the delay allows rivals Vera (VERA) and Otsuka Holdings (OTSKY) (OTSKF) to extend their lead in the IgAN market with their directly competitive, approved drugs. “In a worst-case scenario, the FDA request is looking closer at potential need for IgG monitoring for povetacicept,” Skorney added.

Raymond James analyst Christopher Raymond argued that the insufficient details provided on the reason for the delay are "likely to fuel bearish speculation around the drug’s safety profile.” Raymond, who has a Market Perform rating on VRTX, says he “can’t argue that this program does not now carry a meaningfully higher level of risk.”

data.title: Brazilian stocks surge as Bradesco chairman named finance minister
data.description:
Brazil’s benchmark Ibovespa index (IBOV) jumped 2.6% to hover above 181.5K on Friday, extending a 6.1% rally from the prior session as Bradesco (BBD) board chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco was tapped as finance minister.

The Planalto Palace confirmed Thursday night that Trabuco had accepted President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s invitation, validating market speculation that had fueled gains over recent days.

Investors view the banking executive as likely to curb public spending, easing fiscal concerns that have pressured Brazilian equities amid elevated domestic yields and sluggish business activity since Lula’s re-election.

Many Brazilian stocks, especially those within the financials sector, gapped higher on the news, with Bradesco (BBD) soaring 17% at the time of writing, XP (XP) +18%, Sabesp (SBS) +13%, Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. (ITUB) +13%, Petróleo Brasileiro S.A. (PBR) +7%, StoneCo (STNE) +5%, Companhia Energética de Minas Gerais (CIG) +12%, PagSeguro Digital (PAGS) +7%, Nu Holdings (NU) +8%, Ambev S.A. (ABEV) +8%.

data.title: SA analyst upgrades/downgrades: NVDA, MSFT, GOOG, SNDK
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) received an upgrade following CEO Jensen Huang's rapid reinstatement, while Alphabet (GOOG) saw its rating lifted after a significant price decline brought shares to technical support levels. On the downgrade side, Sandisk (SNDK) faces concerns about a potential NAND cycle peak and intensifying Chinese competition, while Microsoft (MSFT) drew a sell rating as analysts warn that rising depreciation from AI infrastructure spending will erode the company's historically strong margins.

Upgrades

  • Nvidia (NVDA): Upgrade to Buy by Ragmar Rikberg. The analyst cites Jensen Huang's return as CEO and attractive valuation at roughly 9x fiscal 2028 forward earnings as key reasons for the upgrade, noting that NVDA's full-stack strategy deepens ecosystem integration across AI factories, agents, and robotics.

"The ecosystem Jensen has built around Nvidia—and continues to build—is nothing short of exceptional...I think now, assuming Jensen remains at the helm, Nvidia's updated fiscal 2028 outlook, with growth expectations raised from 70% to 75%, provides a reasonable foundation for valuation assessment. In case those growth assumptions hold, Nvidia trades at roughly 9x fiscal 2028 forward earnings."

  • Alphabet (GOOG): Upgrade Sell to Hold by Damir Tokic. The analyst upgraded shares after the stock fell nearly 35% from its May highs, reaching technical support around $260, though fundamental concerns about AI disruption to Google Search and negative free cash flows remain.

"Alphabet is now almost 35% below its all-time highs reached in May—it lost more than a third of its value already. Technically, it reached the support on the 5Y chart right around $260. Thus, it makes sense to temporarily upgrade Alphabet to a Hold (Neutral)."

Downgrades

  • Sandisk (SNDK): Downgrade to Hold by Hunting Alphas. The analyst warns that NAND may be nearing a cyclical peak as Chinese cloud providers cut enterprise SSD orders and consumer demand weakens, while competition from Chinese chipmaker YMTC threatens to pressure global NAND pricing.

"The NAND memory segment is starting to face headwinds that suggest we may be closer to the cyclical peak. Chinese cloud service providers (CSPs) are cutting down their enterprise SSD orders, as they aren't monetizing AI demand as well to justify forking out higher-priced memory. ... I expect this to accelerate a downturn in the NAND cycle and structurally weaken the market shares position of players such as Sandisk."

  • Microsoft (MSFT): Downgrade Hold to Sell by Elina Selianska. The analyst argues that Microsoft's transformation from a zero-production-cost software business to cloud and AI infrastructure will permanently compress margins as depreciation from massive capital spending begins flowing through the income statement.

"Investors still value Microsoft by the standards of an old software giant with zero production cost, while the business is already transforming into infrastructure with an endless cycle of chip replacement and a margin sliding down. When such a restructuring of the business is layered on the tough policy of the Fed, geopolitics, and problems with government debt, holding the capitalization at $3.7 trillion on stubbornness alone won't work."

data.title: Faraday Future announces about $41M investment in FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem
data.description:
• Faraday Future Intelligent Electric (FFAI) announced on Friday an investment in FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem (FFR) worth around $41 million.
  • FFR said that it filed a preliminary Schedule 14C with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 25, marking the completion of all material matters required of both parties post deal closing.  
  • As of November 25, 2026, FFAI beneficially held roughly 14.7 million shares of FFR common stock, representing around 53% of outstanding common shares.
  • Following completion of the deal, FFAI would hold around 80.1 million common shares, representing about 75% of the resulting outstanding common stock of FFR.
  • All newly issued FFR shares received by FFAI in the transaction are subject to an 18-month lock-up period.

data.title: Wall Street firmly in green as it looks to end volatile week on a high
data.description:
Wall Street rose on Friday as it hoped to close out a volatile week with a winning session, while Treasury yields moved higher following the Thanksgiving holiday break.

S&P 500 (SP500) +1.1%, the Dow (DJI) +1%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +1.4%.

Wall Street returned to trading after the Thanksgiving holiday, with investors looking to end a turbulent week on a positive note. The market has experienced sharp swings, with significant gains followed by heavy selloffs.

On the economic front, investors will monitor the Federal Reserve's balance sheet report. U.S. stock markets will also close early on Friday for the Black Friday holiday session.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 4.2 basis points to 4.70%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 5.1 basis points to 4.92%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) rose 5.1 basis points to 5.30%.
